chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Five Words th
spiritual_reading:
They direct the mind toward the inmost Divine, acknowledging it as the source of all life, yet confessing that it cannot be comprehended by any created understanding nor defined by any determinate idea; therefore no one can grasp its quality as if from self.

They then speak of a distinct proceeding of that same Divine, an office of mediation by which life is made present and communicated. This mediation is understood as a living operation that bears the quality of the source while remaining subordinate to it, so that it can be received by those below. For this reason they describe it as a paternal principle relative to what is derived from it, yet they still recognize the inmost Divine as the first and unoriginated source above it.

fills.notes: The sentence is defining what ‘they’ call the Father and why the name is used; the substrate voice is impersonal and descriptive, so a neutral collective subject (‘Those who…’) fits the correspondential intent: minds directed toward the inmost Divine without preaching.

fills.fill: life, the one who is before all
fills.notes: The Father is identified as Life itself and as prior to all derivations. The spiritual translation stresses the unoriginated source; ‘before all’ preserves the oldest-layer cosmological register (priority of principle) without later devotional coloring.
The point is the incomprehensibility of the inmost Divine: no created understanding can comprehend or define it. ‘Whom no one knows his name’ expresses that ungraspability as to quality.

Keeps the given reconstruction, which matches the structural listing of ‘first… second…’ names and preserves the technical title ‘Third Ambassador’ as the mediating proceeding described in the spiritual translation.

Correspondentially this figure is the proceeding mediation by which life is made present and communicated. ‘Living’ ties directly to ‘of life’ and avoids later institutional framing; ‘envoy’ matches ‘Ambassador’ while keeping the older impersonal cosmological tone.

fills.fill: all that is derived from him
fills.notes: The text calls him ‘father of …’ in the sense of a paternal principle relative to what proceeds. This fill makes explicit the correspondential relation of source-to-derived without importing later moral or ecclesial terms.

The clause must preserve subordination: the mediator bears the quality of the source but is not the first. ‘Yet he is after the first Father’ states discrete order of origin, matching the spiritual translation (‘subordinate… still recognize the inmost Divine as the first’).

assessment: Most gaps can be restored at the level of cosmological sense because the chapter is a definition-chain: (1) the inmost Father as unnameable Life beyond comprehension, then (2) a proceeding mediator called the Third Ambassador, paternal toward what derives yet subordinate to the First. Exact connective particles are less constrained, but the required correspondential relations (unoriginated source; proceeding mediation; derived order) tightly limit the viable restorations.
